chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'One who fears robbers and wild beasts prays the prayer of al-Muwaqafah by gesture while on his mount.' I said: 'Do I understand that if the one praying is not in a state of wudu, what should he do when he cannot dismount?' He said: 'He performs tayammum from the felt of his saddle or his mount or from the saddle-ring of his mount, for there is dust in it, and he prays and makes the prostration lower than the bowing, and he does not turn his body towards the Qibla, but wherever his mount turns, provided that he faces the Qibla with the first Takbir when he sets out.'

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: By gesture (pointing with head or eyes, indicating partial prostration)
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْمُوَاقَفَةِ: Prayer of the Station/Waiting (a specific form of prayer during fear)
key_terms.مَعْرَفَةُ دَابَّتِهِ: The saddle-ring or stirrup of his mount

ai.seo_question: How does one pray while mounted during times of fear if they cannot dismount or perform full ablution?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of Zurara, clarifies the practical application of Salat al-Khawf for travelers on mount, emphasizing that the Qibla orientation is determined by the mount's direction at the opening Takbir rather than continuous facing. It further details the concession of performing tayammum using dust from the saddle or mount when water is unavailable or dismounting is impossible, reflecting the Shia principle of ease (taysir) in times of genuine fear. This ruling underscores the flexibility in ritual purity and posture, allowing prostration to be lower than bowing to maintain stability while mounted.
